observed_evidence: Reuters reported on 2026-09-16 that Saudi Arabia is offering additional Arab Light, Arab Medium and Arab Heavy crude to Asian term buyers via ship-to-ship loading off Sohar, Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz, after attacks damaged the East-West Pipeline and halted Yanbu loadings.

Reuters reported Saudi Gulf loadings at Ras Tanura and Juaymah had risen to roughly 4 million bpd, while at least one Asian buyer had received a delay notice and some European September cargoes had been cancelled.
Reuters reported on 2026-09-16 that Russia decided to extend diesel-export restrictions for producers through the end of October, following refinery disruptions and domestic fuel-market pressure.
semantic_interpretation: Saudi use of Oman ship-to-ship loading is a partial mitigation channel for the crude-supply shock and lowers the probability of complete export impairment, but it does not restore Yanbu or the East-West Pipeline and therefore does not remove Hormuz/Red Sea logistics risk. Russia's extension of diesel-export restrictions increases persistence of the separate refined-product shock and can sustain diesel cracks, freight costs and energy inflation. Net global energy risk remains very high but is less one-sided than the prior snapshot because Saudi alternative routing is now observed.
